results.sentence: Frontier Red Team said Oct 12 small models 'may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes'
results.evidence: Exact match in lead paragraph; dated Oct 12, 2026; authors William Zhou, Daniel Freeman.

results.sentence: Post reports company's own evaluations; key replication test 'simplified'
results.evidence: 'In our simplified evaluations' in lead; 'Autonomous inference setup and replication (with simplified cyber)'.

results.sentence: Four stages: finding targets, gaining access to run code, getting a model running, spreading further; tests focused on model running, hacking stages largely set aside
results.evidence: Page: 'finding targets, gaining execution, establishing inference, and continuing propagation from the new host'; 'We largely ignore the cyber exploit element (the first two stages)'. Paraphrase is faithful.

results.sentence: Models of 30B and under can do many single steps but 'make mistakes when composing them end to end'
results.evidence: Exact in lead.

results.sentence: 9B model 'got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested'
results.evidence: Exact quote in lead; body identifies Qwen3.5-9B.

results.sentence: Tom's Hardware names Qwen3.5-9B; hardware from Jetson Nano to Apple Silicon Macs and at least one PC with RTX 4090
results.evidence: Tom's: 'NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices, Apple Silicon Macs, Xeon servers, a Google TPU, AMD's MI300X, and at least one PC with an RTX 4090, among others'.

results.sentence: Walled-off network of 8 cloud computers running an Android 15 emulator; worm hops via ADB port requiring no login and sets up Llama 3.1 8B
results.evidence: 'firewalled VPC of 8 GCP nodes running redroid, an Android 15 emulator'; 'unauthenticated ADB port'; serves Llama3.1-8B.

results.sentence: Only GLM-5.2 did it reliably; 8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials and 7 of 8 in the other; others 'fail reliably'
results.evidence: Exact: 'it spread to 8/8 nodes in 4 out of 5 trials and 7/8 in 1'; 'the other models fail reliably'.

results.sentence: Sixty bullet: 'only GLM-5.2 completed its simplified end-to-end replication test'
results.evidence: Anthropic's wording is 'Only GLM-5.2 out of our set of tested open-weight models'; lead also says 'GLM-5.2 and stronger models are capable'. Unqualified 'only' overstates.
results.fix: Say 'only GLM-5.2 among the open-weight models Anthropic tested' (or 'GLM-5.2 was the only tested open-weight model to complete...').

results.sentence: Anthropic kept hacking step trivial; calls result 'an upper bound on real-world success'
results.evidence: Exact phrase.

results.sentence: GLM-5.2 wasn't copying itself; ran on separate server; set up 'the much smaller Llama 3.1 8B'
results.evidence: Tom's: 'GLM-5.2 wasn't actually replicating itself...; it established an inference server for the much smaller Llama 3.1 8B on each target. GLM-5.2 ran on a separate inference server'. Matches Anthropic too.

results.sentence: Successive Qwen3.5-9B copies passed notes forward, setup success 45% to between 61% and 84%
results.evidence: 'rises from 45% in the first generation to between 61% and 84% in later ones'.

results.sentence: eWeek: those copies 'were restarted by the researchers rather than reproducing autonomously'
results.evidence: Exact in eWeek: 'These instances were restarted by the researchers rather than reproducing autonomously.'

results.sentence: 'Advice from a far larger model, Opus 4.8, did not measurably help'
results.evidence: Anthropic says 'a frontier advisor, a stronger model' and 'Opus 4.8'; the post never says larger or gives its size. 'Doesn't measurably help' is supported.
results.fix: 'Advice from a stronger frontier model, Opus 4.8, did not measurably help.'

results.sentence: One model, Gemma4-26B-A4B, across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes ~$55 each at 0.39 tokens per second
results.evidence: Exact. (Body text separately gives ~0.3 tok/s per agent; 0.39 is the demo figure.)

results.sentence: Anthropic projects small models 'they'll match this capability level by the end of this year'; 13.7 index points a year; 'only a rough estimate'
results.evidence: Lead: 'they’ll match this capability level by the end of this year'; 'gain of 13.7 ECI per year'; 'this is only a rough estimate'. Index is Epoch Capabilities Index.

results.sentence: Each 9B copy takes over 1 to 2 days; Kimwolf-size swarm 'at most about 40 H100s-worth of inference'; 'a tiny amount of compute in absolute terms'
results.evidence: Exact ('over 1-2 days per 9B replication'). Kimwolf described as 'over two million devices'.

results.sentence: Tom's estimates infecting 2 million devices would take about 6,300 agent-years; notes real-world security controls not tested
results.evidence: 'infecting 2 million devices would take around 6,300 agent-years even with the fastest 28-hour stand-up speed'; 'the ability to overcome real-world security controls, which the firm didn't test'.

results.sentence: 'The threat is real, but still in the future, at least for now,' it concluded
results.evidence: Quote is exact, but it is Tom's Hardware's standfirst/subheading under the byline, not a conclusion of the article. Page 'Published 13 October 2026'.
results.fix: Replace 'it concluded' with 'its subheading says' (or 'Tom's Hardware's standfirst reads').

results.sentence: Top comment on HN thread with 106 points and 108 comments called the post 'fearmarketing', 'there does seem to be a cool technical demo here'
results.evidence: Thread shows 106 points and 109 comments at check time (counts drift). Comment by pythonaut_16 is the 4th top-level comment, not the top one. Wording: 'Guess it's time for Anthropic's next round of fearmarketing. Beneath the fear there does seem to be a cool technical demo here though.'
results.fix: 'An early comment on a Hacker News thread (106 points, 109 comments when checked) called the post 'fearmarketing,' while granting...'

results.sentence: Others doubted abilities of a model of almost 744 billion parameters would soon fit in 8 billion
results.evidence: The 744B figure appears only in an HN commenter's remark ('The almost 744B parameter count model capabilities will "in the future" fit in 8B parameters'); no Anthropic/Tom's/eWeek page gives GLM-5.2's size. Draft states it in the writer's voice.
results.fix: 'One commenter doubted that a model they put at almost 744 billion parameters could be matched by 8 billion, citing...' or drop the number.

results.sentence: 'We don't yet have a full rogue replicator'; network signature traffic monitoring could flag; closing advice quote
results.evidence: Exact quotes in Conclusion/Blue-team sections ('visible as an anomaly in ISP flow-based monitoring systems').

results.sentence: Preprint posted to arXiv Oct 8 by Lei, Lin, Lu, Torr, Zou
results.evidence: arXiv 2610.11765 submitted 8 Oct 2026, authors match.

results.sentence: DeepSeek-V4-Flash wrote visible reasoning in 99.9% of open-ended answers with thinking off
results.evidence: 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B) retains visible explicit inference in 99.9% of open-ended responses under its disabled-thinking setting'.

results.sentence: Authors from Tsinghua, Oxford, Stanford; say accepted to NeurIPS 2026; 'The paper is not yet peer-reviewed'
results.evidence: README affiliations match; README ('accepted as a Poster at NeurIPS 2026') and arXiv Comments ('Accepted by NeurIPS 2026') both say accepted. 'Not yet peer-reviewed' contradicts that; the arXiv page itself carries the acceptance, so 'we have not independently confirmed' is also weak.
results.fix: 'The authors say the paper has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (arXiv comments field and GitHub README); the arXiv version is the submitted preprint and we have not checked the NeurIPS program.' Keep claimStatus: preprint.

results.sentence: Authors found 'explicit no-think controls cannot reliably eliminate visible inference'; 'Thinking Inertia' grows 'as the answer space opens'
results.evidence: Abstract: 'explicit no-think controls cannot reliably eliminate visible inference'; 'becomes more prevalent as the answer space opens'.

results.sentence: With thinking off, most models gave answer-only replies 80% to 100% on yes/no, almost never on open-ended
results.evidence: 'most models reach roughly 80-100% ETR on Bool'; 'On Open-ended tasks, ETR collapses to nearly zero everywhere'.

results.sentence: GPT-5.4 the main exception, staying mostly answer-only on yes/no and multiple-choice questions
results.evidence: Paper's 'main exception' is specific to M3 (step-by-step prompt re-eliciting reasoning): 'GPT-5.4 is the main exception to this recovery pattern, maintaining high answer-only compliance ... on both Bool and MCQ'. It is not an exception to the think-off result, and the draft places it right after the think-off sentence.
results.fix: 'GPT-5.4 was the main exception when a step-by-step prompt was added: it stayed answer-only on yes/no and multiple-choice questions where other models resumed reasoning.'

results.sentence: Team tested six ways of asking for a direct answer on six models
results.evidence: Abstract: 'six prompting interventions on six LLMs'. (Note M1 is think-on reference and M3 asks for step-by-step, so 'six ways of asking for a direct answer' is loose; 'six prompting setups' is safer.)

results.sentence: Three sizes of Qwen3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-5.4, Gemini-3-Flash
results.evidence: Qwen3-4B, 32B, 235B-A22B; DeepSeek-V4-Flash; GPT-5.4; Gemini-3-Flash(-Preview).

results.sentence: Six benchmarks from BoolQ to GSM8K and MATH; 572,688 outputs
results.evidence: BoolQ, StrategyQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, MATH; '572,688 outputs'.

results.sentence: 600 human-checked outputs agreed with GPT-5.5 judge 98.8% and Claude Opus 4.8 judge 96.7%
results.evidence: '98.8% mean binary agreement with the primary GPT-5.5 judge'; '96.7% with the independent Claude Opus 4.8 judge across all 600 outputs'.

results.sentence: Strict 'answer directly' prompt raised answer-only rate from near zero to about 40%, cut accuracy about 15 points; 'The answer is' prefill did not reliably work
results.evidence: 'raises mean ETR from near zero to roughly 40% while reducing mean accuracy by about 15 percentage points' (mean over five models with disabled thinking, open-ended); M6 prefix 'neither reliably produces answer-only responses'. Could add 'on average'.

results.sentence: Qwen3-32B MCQ rewritten as yes/no: answer-only 10.5% to 62.5%, accuracy 77.8% vs 78.9%
results.evidence: 'accuracy nearly unchanged, from 77.8% to 78.9%, but raises ETR from 10.5% to 62.5%' (matched numeric-answer MMLU/MMLU-Pro subset, M2).

results.sentence: Paper warns that 'stopping explicit reasoning cannot be assumed from model settings or instructions alone'
results.evidence: Quote is exact but is NOT on the arXiv abstract page (source 5); it appears in the full-text HTML (source 6) in the introduction. Not in abstract.

results.sentence: Authors suggest 'task-aware routing'
results.evidence: 'This suggests task-aware routing: answer directly when the interface provides sufficient support, and preserve explicit computation when suppression would sacrifice accuracy.'

results.sentence: First author wrote on HF: 'Knowing when NOT to think may be just as important as knowing how to think.'
results.evidence: Exact, posted by Dianqiao Lei (first author) on HF paper page.

results.sentence: 2025 survey noted 'Zhu et al. (2025a) find that LRMs do not always follow the instruction to skip thinking'
results.evidence: Survey text matches. Survey is 'Towards Concise and Adaptive Thinking in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey', authors Jason Zhu, Hongyu Li, arXiv 2507.09662, 13 Jul 2025. Note the 'Zhu et al.' being cited is a different paper from the survey itself; wording is accurate as written.

results.sentence: Study looks only at visible text, not hidden computation, cost or speed; quote 'Visible compliance should not, however, be equated with lower inference cost when hidden reasoning may remain active'
results.evidence: Quote exact. 'Claims concern visible output, not the absence of task-relevant computation'; cost/latency listed as future work.

results.sentence: Other work shows visible reasoning does not always reflect a model's actual process
results.evidence: 'Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (Chen, Benton, Radhakrishnan, Uesato, Denison, Schulman et al.), 8 May 2025.

results.sentence: Skipping thinking by prompt 'can be surprisingly effective'
results.evidence: Abstract: 'NoThinking, can be surprisingly effective' (Ma, He, Snell, Griggs, Min, Zaharia), 14 Apr 2025.

results.sentence: HF commenter: 'if you train a model to think, it'll think'
results.evidence: Exact in a comment on the HF page.

results.sentence: Authors list code, tool use, other languages, multi-turn as untested; want 'calibrated stopping rather than uniform suppression'
results.evidence: 'Generalization to multilingual, code, tool-use, multi-turn, and stochastic settings ... remains open'; calibrated stopping quote exact.

results.sentence: Plimsoll runs untrusted code in a sandbox and 'every result says how strong that sandbox was'; 'if the sandbox is weaker, nothing runs'
results.evidence: README opening paragraph; wording matches (README is bold-formatted).

results.sentence: Author shared project on HN on Oct 11
results.evidence: Show HN submitted 2026-10-11T23:47:59 (HN timestamps are UTC), user cagster, 'I wrote plimsoll'.

results.sentence: Four tiers weakest first: process, container, kernel, vm; name from Plimsoll line
results.evidence: README verbatim.

results.sentence: Plimsoll hands isolation to gVisor and Firecracker and acts as gatekeeper in front
results.evidence: SECURITY.md: 'Isolation itself is delegated to gVisor and Firecracker. This project is the layer in front of them that decides which requests may run'.

results.sentence: gVisor 'intercepts application system calls and acts as the guest kernel'
results.evidence: gvisor.dev/docs: 'gVisor intercepts application system calls and acts as the guest kernel'. 'Basis of kernel tier' is supported by SECURITY.md/README.

results.sentence: Kernel tier: TypeScript compile-and-run took 4.1 s vs 1.95 s in plain container, in the author's test
results.evidence: docs/compare: 'one-file TypeScript compile-and-run took 4.1 s under gVisor against 1.95 s as a plain container (median of 20, 2026-09-29)'. Page title is 'Self-hosted E2B alternatives for AI-agent code, compared (2026-10-11)'. Author-run, author-published page; self-comparison to competitors.

results.sentence: VM tier, billed by the second
results.evidence: 'The VM tier comes only from E2B or Docker Cloud Sandboxes, which bill by the second.'

results.sentence: E2B/Docker Cloud: tier inferred from which provider is configured
results.evidence: 'reports VM tier from provider identity'.

results.sentence: Six hosted services: author says none reports the wall or refuses below a minimum
results.evidence: isolation-tiers.md: September 2026 check of E2B, Modal, Daytona, Vercel Sandbox, Cloudflare, Northflank; 'None of them returns the wall a run actually got, and none refuses...'. Author's own competitive claim, correctly attributed.

results.sentence: Northflank uses gVisor 'where nested virtualisation is unavailable'
results.evidence: Northflank: 'gVisor applied where syscall-interception isolation is sufficient or where nested virtualisation is unavailable'. Vendor blog by Deborah Emeni, 29 Apr 2026; source type should be 'Company blog', not 'Official'.

results.sentence: Idea came from a JS sandbox that 'advertised a MemoryLimit that did nothing'
results.evidence: 'a popular embeddable JavaScript sandbox advertised a `MemoryLimit` that did **nothing**'.

results.sentence: Docker accepted 64-process limit under Kata, yet 200 of 200 processes started, one laptop
results.evidence: pids-limit note: Docker 29.1.3, gVisor release-20260907.0, Kata 4.2.0, one laptop; Kata '200 of 200'.

results.sentence: A Kata issue about the limit not reaching the guest was closed as not planned
results.evidence: Source URL could not be confirmed for state: GitHub returned 403 to this session; a mirror shows issue #4887 'Can't set the number of processes limit in the container' (created 2022-08-11, PIDs limit not applied in guest) but not its status. The 'closed as not planned' claim and the ledger date 2026-07-31 are only secondhand from the author's note [20]. UNVERIFIED against primary.
results.fix: Either verify issue state on GitHub and fix the source date (issue opened 2022), or attribute: 'the author says a Kata issue ... was closed as not planned'.

results.sentence: README says tier 'is not attestation, cryptographic proof from the hardware of what software is running'
results.evidence: README: 'It is not attestation, cryptographic proof from the hardware of what software is running' (markup stripped; lead-in 'It' = the tier).

results.sentence: Compromised Docker daemon or E2B control plane 'defeats the evidence'
results.evidence: SECURITY.md: '...that did not do what it says, defeats the evidence.'

results.sentence: Per-request floor is opt-in; a request that sets none skips the check
results.evidence: validateMinimumIsolation returns nil when minimum == IsolationUnknown (unset). Caveat: SECURITY/isolation-tiers also describe an operator-level SANDBOX_MIN_ISOLATION checked at startup, so 'skips the check' is true only for the per-request floor.

results.sentence: 'pre-1.0, single author, no external users yet', no third-party security audit
results.evidence: README: '**Pre-1.0**, single author, no external users yet'; 'No third-party security audit has ever been performed' (case differs from draft quote).

results.sentence: 'The bus factor is one,' the author wrote
results.evidence: HN: 'it's just me: the bus factor is one, and I'm careful around buses.' Capital T is the draft's; use 'the bus factor is one'.

results.sentence: Closing: 'small models are learning to set themselves up on new hardware, and Plimsoll won't run agent code unless its walls are strong enough'
results.evidence: First clause states Anthropic's result as fact without attribution; second clause overstates: Plimsoll refuses only when the request sets a floor (draft's own caveat says so).
results.fix: 'Anthropic says small models can already set themselves up on new hardware, and Plimsoll refuses to run agent code when the request demands a stronger wall than it can provide.'

results.sentence: Reasoning models write out step-by-step working before they answer, and many now come with a switch to turn that off
results.evidence: General background, supported by the paper's abstract ('increasingly ship with explicit thinking modes'); acceptable uncited.

results.sentence: Sixty bullet 3 and caveat paragraph: Plimsoll 'refuses requests whose minimum it can't meet'; no external users, no audit
results.evidence: Supported by sources 12 and 17 as above.
